cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Find the Real Authority
cards.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I permit you to book our trip, who can still cancel it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee approved it. May I pay before we lose the coach?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may check who controls the deposit. Whose objection would stop the payment?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer's. She's away, but her deputy has the bank login.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I authorize one more question for the deputy: can she release it alone, or does the treasurer still have to say yes?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 withholds booking permission; A3 permits an authority check instead of payment; A5 authorizes a narrower deputy probe after B4, joining hierarchy to finding real control.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 committee approval does not settle deposit control; A3 asks that distinction, and A5 tests whether B4 access is enough.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to secure the coach and B4 supplies a practical workaround; A3 takes charge without denying that information.

heightening.evidence: B4 absent treasurer and available deputy cause A5 to distinguish physical access from authorization, a more precise version of the same inquiry.

specificity.evidence: A1 trip booking and B2 possible loss of coach establish the task; B4 fictional login is an access fact, not actual credential material.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 grants checking rather than requested payment; A5 grants yet another question. The repeated restrictive permission is playable but more dry than surprising.
